title: Calc chain reduces 2^n mod 7 to 2^(n % 3) (IMO 1964 Q1)
intent: Show that 2^n mod 7 depends only on n % 3 by rewriting 2^n as 2^(3*(n/3) + n%3), then pushing the period 2^3 ≡ 1 (mod 7) through a four-link calc chain, ending at 2^(n % 3). Each link closes with one tactic and no auxiliary lemma.

applicability.goal_shape: a congruence a ≡ b [MOD m] (or equality) where a can be rewritten so that a periodic subterm (here 2^3 mod 7 = 1) appears, collapsing a to a residue b that depends on n only through n % k
applicability.use_when: the goal reduces to a chain of equalities and congruences each provable by one rewrite or normalising tactic; the period (here 2^3 ≡ 1 [MOD 7]) is a closed computation that decide closes inline
applicability.avoid_when: a link needs a non-rewrite argument (induction, case analysis, a named lemma) that will not sit on one calc line; the period is not computable by decide (symbolic base or modulus); the congruence does not respect the operation used in a link

claims.claim: The whole proof of two_pow_mod_seven is a single four-link calc chain and nothing else: after let t := n % 3, each link closes inline with one tactic (rw [Nat.div_add_mod]; rw [pow_add, pow_mul]; gcongr; decide; ring), and no auxiliary lemma or have intervenes, so the children are exactly these four links.
The module docstring states the period that the chain encodes: "For (a), we find that the order of 2 mod 7 is 3. Therefore for (b), it suffices to check n = 0, 1, 2."

two_pow_mod_seven is referenced at two further sites in the same file — line 45 in imo1964_q1a and line 54 in imo1964_q1b — so the chain's conclusion 2^n ≡ 2^(n % 3) [MOD 7] is the exact lemma both later proofs need.
claims.evidence: read of the copied file Archive/Imo/Imo1964Q1.lean, lines 45 and 54

claims.claim: The calc-chain move is used twice more in the same file: imo1964_q1a (lines 42-47) chains equivalences over ↔ and imo1964_q1b (lines 53-55) chains congruences over ≡ [MOD 7], so the move works for more than one relation kind.

metrics.how_counted: lines 28-33 of the copied file; children = the four calc links; reuse_sites = references to two_pow_mod_seven at lines 45 and 54, counted by reading the file

consequences: The chain replaces one congruence with four sub-goals (the links), but none is a named lemma: each link's justification is an inline tactic, and the calc elaborator supplies transitivity, so no separate transitivity proof is owed. The one substantive obligation is the period 2^3 ≡ 1 [MOD 7], discharged inline by decide inside link 3; if the base or modulus were symbolic, that link would not close and would have to be extracted into its own lemma. The chain mixes = and ≡ links, which typechecks only because = implies the congruence reflexively; reordering the relations would break it.
